main_text.p: liquæ antem quæ circa eam sunt stellæ القلادص vel القلادص quod Camelas juvenculas & minores denotat, monente AlKazwinio, qui & eam expresse عين الثور Oculum Tauri, vocari asserit. Author libri التبيان sic eandem describit هو كوكب احمر معه الدبران اربعة كواكب انا وصلتها بها كانت كالدال علي هذه الصفة i.e. AlDabaran est stella rutilans, lucida, & cum ea quatuor alia quas ubi ei adjunxerit, figurâ referent literam ט hoc modo[?]. Quænam ergò fuerit stella quæ cultûs objectum patet, at qui tandem ejus cultores? In duobus exemplaribus nomine Misam insigniuntur, quod inter tribus aut familias Arabum illustres non reperio. Sunt quæ literarum ductu non longè recedunt, تميم Tamim & تيم Tayem, & جشم Josham, & جشيم Jashim, sed proximè accedit ميتم Mitam.

Lachmus & Jodamus Jovem ]ita scil. legendum, non Martem. quod nescio, quomodo calami-festinantis errore, irrepserit. De المشتري autem, quo nomine Jovis stellam appellant, Etymo, quid doceat AlMakrizi in iis quæ supra dicta sunt, vidimus. Monet AlKazwini vocari eandem ab Astrologis السعد الاكبر i.e. Bona fortuna major seu maxima, respectu scil Veneris, quæ السعد الاصغر i.e. Fortuna minor dicitur, quia (inquit) est في فوق الزهرة السعادة seu felicitate Venerem superat, adeoque illi الخيرات الكثيرة والسعادات العظيمة i.e. Bona multa, & felicitates magnas, ascribunt. Eodem spectat quod asserunt Hebræorum Magistri vocari apud Arabes Jovis fidus גד Gad quod מזל טוב seu Fortunam bonam interpretantur: certè Arabes (ut videre est apud Alsaub: & AlFiruzabad, &c.) الجد red-duntR Mosch. citant Ab. Ezr. ad Gen. 30. & Ps. 65. et Radic. ib. & in radic.

page.notes: Left margin note transcribed as printed; "Ab.Ezr al" and "1/31 65" are doubtful readings, possibly "ad" and "Ps." Word "reddunt" is broken at the line end, and the printed hyphen is uncertain, so it is written as "red-dunt". The Arabic words after "vel" and "quod" in the first lines, the Hebrew letter ט after "literam", and the Arabic pieces in the diagram-like line "هذه الصفة" are copied as seen but may contain small errors. The page ends mid-paragraph, so the text continues on the next page. Some Arabic vowel marks are not clearly visible and are left out.
